Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Pakistan's second innings. The two umpires and the English players head out to the centre. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique to open the innings for Pakistan. Chris Woakes has the red cherry in hand. Away we go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

With the pitch not exhibiting the expected wear and tear for a Day 4 surface, Pakistan will be keen to make a solid start to their innings. Given that we’re likely to have around 20 minutes of play before Tea, the primary objective for Pakistan will be to remain unscathed during this crucial phase. Time is of the essence, and England have set themselves up with four full sessions and a few overs here in the second session to have a crack at Pakistan. Back in a bit for Pakistan's reply.

The declaration has finally come, much to the relief of Pakistan. End of an absolute run fest from England. Barring the skipper Ollie Pope, all English batters imposed themselves and cashed in to pile the misery on the Pakistani attack. England end up with 823 on the board with a lead of 267 runs. As they walk off the field, the Pakistani players wear a tired look, understandably so after fielding for 150 overs in the sweltering heat of Multan, with not much going their way throughout the innings. While the bowlers can finally put their feet up, the openers will need to be switched on right from ball one against this English attack.

Good length at the stumps. Carse pushes it back at the bowler. And, finally, Ollie Pope the stand-in English skipper signals for a declaration. Pakistan batted for 149 overs, and scored 556, while England batted for just one over more, and have mounted up a mammoth total breaching the 800-run mark.

Commentary.Commentary: DAY 4, SESSION 2 - Welcome back for the post-Lunch session of Day 4! The sun continues to beat down heavily over Multan and out walk the two umpires. Pakistani players are in a team huddle near the ropes before spreading out to the field. Probably discussing the strategies on what their approach is going to be from here. Joe Root, unbeaten on 259, along with Harry Brook batting on 218 to resume their innings. England lead by 102 and it will be Aamer Jamal (21-0-101-1) to resume the proceedings for Pakistan with the ball. Here we go...
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

Starting the day trailing by 64 runs, England's lead has now stretched to 102. One thing is for certain - England will push for a result, and the key question is how many overs will be enough to bowl Pakistan out on this docile surface. With this in mind, expect them to put their foot down after Lunch. That said, considering this is just the first match of the series, England will be keen to manage their workload and won't want to bowl too many overs in the second innings in this heat. If England go hard, chances will be created for Pakistan, but they must hold on and support their bowlers effectively. Join us again for the start of the second session at 7.40 am GMT.

Only one chance was created throughout the session, but it was squandered by Babar Azam when he dropped Joe Root on 186. After that missed opportunity, Pakistan’s energy visibly dropped, and they merely went through the motions for the remainder of the session. First, Root, and then Brook, brought up their respective double centuries – Root’s sixth of his career and Brook’s maiden double ton. While a few deliveries from Salman Agha showed some grip, the absence of Abrar Ahmed, who has been hospitalised due to fever, left Pakistan a key spin option short, further compounding their woes.

Bat continues to dominate the ball in Multan, resulting in another session bossed by England in this Test. 166 runs were scored in the session from 29 overs at a rate of 5.72 runs per over, and it came with utmost ease. Earlier, Pakistan found some encouragement when a couple of deliveries seemingly deviated off the cracks and beat the bat, but those moments of hope quickly vanished as the conditions eased. Harry Brook and Joe Root comfortably settled into their rhythm, effortlessly piling on the runs and maintaining England's stronghold on the game.
Just a little hint of turn on that one, spinning on the pads, on the back of a length, Brook clips it to deep fine for a comfortable single. AND THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 4!

Commentary.Commentary: Well then, all in readiness for Day 4 to commence! The sun is shining bright and to its full glory over Multan. The Barmy Army folks are out there and chirping in the stands as well to support their team. Now, the umpires are out to the middle. Pakistani players also take their respective fielding positions. Joe Root, unbeaten on 176, and Harry Brook on 141 are the overnight batters for England. Shaheen Afridi (19-1-88-1) will start the proceedings for Pakistan with the ball. And, here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Ramiz Raja is near the deck. He starts by informing that the grass has been taken off and the cracks have started to open up a bit. Feels that this surface is a little bit abrasive now but there are no demons yet. Tells that it will be important for the batters to cover the line but more than the technical, it will be about the mental aspect from the Pakistani perspective who have not batted well in the recent past on Days 4 and 5 of the Test.

Pakistan still has the cushion of the early morning hour. As batters often need time to regain their rhythm after the overnight break, this period of initial rustiness could be exploited given the ball is still semi-new and that it has started to reverse. If executed well, this Pakistani pace attack has all the potential to run through the lineup, but it’s all about giving it all. An action-packed Day 4 is set to begin shortly. Stay tuned.

Pakistan's bowling strategy has strangely been notably conservative, showing little tactical variation to disrupt the opposition’s rhythm. The lack of spin and grip on the surface rendered Abrar Ahmed's prolonged spell from one end largely ineffective, inadvertently allowing the English batters to settle comfortably. They used as many as seven bowlers. Even the introduction of the second new ball failed to inject sharpness into the pace attack, its impact seemingly blunted by the unresponsively dead pitch. Adding to their frustrations was one umpire’s call off Naseem’s bowling, or be it the bails not coming off when the ball ricocheted off Brook’s body.

The catalyst for this resurgence was Joe Root's masterful innings of 176. Taking to the crease mere moments into England's response, on just the ninth ball, Root orchestrated a brilliant recovery. He forged three century-plus partnerships, first with Crawley, then Duckett, and finally Brook, each alliance crucial in steering England away from what could have been a dire situation. A lot of records were toppled, notably Root becoming England’s top run-getter in Tests, surpassing Sir Alastair Cook and moving into fifth place on the overall all-time rankings while Brook’s brisk century was the sixth of his career and fourth against Pakistan.

After toiling in the heat of Multan for almost six sessions, England have strongly bounced back in this contest now with the bat. The Bazballers haven’t been reluctant to stay obedient to their approach one bit. England mounted an impressive comeback against Pakistan's formidable 556. They’re now just 64 runs behind and still have 7 wickets in hand with a fair bit of batting left. Their aim would be to bat for the whole day and extend the lead to a considerable margin. To cement how bad conditions are for the bowlers, out of 101 overs bowled by Pakistan, only a solitary maiden over was bowled, by Shaheen.

Typically, the third day of a Test match introduces new challenges as the pitch deteriorates. However, the Multan surface remained stubbornly flat, with minimal rough patches. While some reverse swing emerged for seamers late on day three, it brought little success. The road-like pitch continues to offer minimal assistance to bowlers, defying the usual expectations of wear and tear.

Hello and a warm welcome from Multan for the coverage of Day 4 in this series opener between Pakistan and England. After the first two sedate days, things moved quite dramatically and at a brisk pace on the third day. To sum up things in brief, conditions have been torturous for the bowlers.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, there isn't much to write home about the Pakistan bowlers but a couple of them did give it their all. Aamer Jamal was the pick of the bowlers but failed to hit that hard length consistently enough and then Naseem Shah bowled a lovely spell late in the days, challenging the set batters. The big task for the home team is that they have to pull off something different at the start of Day 4 if they are to get back in the game whereas this duo of Root and Brook will be eyeing their double hundreds. Join us on Thursday, 10 October at 5 am GMT for the action on Day 4. Cheers!

Ben Duckett is up for a quick chat. He says that he is doing fine now. Says it was a bit sore yesterday, and the injury dissipated last night. On batting at number 4, he says he really didn't know what to do on this pitch but while batting he realised that it's a good batting track and you don't want to leave to many balls on such wickets. Mentions it did not spin much. Tells they have all day tomorrow to surpass Pakistan and then aim to bowl them out on Day 5. On being asked about Root, he says it is difficult to put the appreciations in words about him and they are just witnessing his greatness. Ends up by saying he has been in the form of his life recently.

Once Harry Brook joined Joe Root at the crease, the pair simply didn't look back and the former came out playing his shots. The pair kept on piling on the runs and Pakistan's lead spinner, Abrar Ahmed was taken to the cleaners. Root broke a few records throughout the day, the first one was surpassing Sir Alastair Cook as the leading run-scorer for England in Tests as he joined the top 5 batters in the world as well. Then he went on to score his 35th Test ton, joining the top 6 in the world. Harry Brook also breached the three-figure mark and the duo have put on 243 runs for the 4th wicket, which is a record stand for England against Pakistan for the 4th wicket.

England began the day with just one wicket down and the overnight batters started in fine form but soon enough Zak Crawley played a poor shot and got out. After that Ben Duckett came out to bat and it didn't feel like he had injured his left thumb as he smashed the ball to all parts of the ground. Duckett too, like Crawley couldn't convert the fifty into a ton and got out. Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the final session of Day 3. The players are already out in the middle. Joe Root and Harry Brook unbeaten with a solid 106-run stand to resume their innings. Abrar Ahmed to bowl the first over of the session with England trailing by 203 more runs. Here we go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

All in all, it is still a batting paradise and there's distantly no sign of the pitch becoming a rank turner or even a huge extractor of swing. The fact that only one maiden over has been bowled in the span of 70 overs proves the challenging conditions faced by the bowlers on this surface. England will come out with the same intent and shrink the opposition's lead as they still have a few batters to come out. Pakistan will need to get their act together and find breakthroughs by creating chances. A couple of wickets or more and they will be right back in the game. At this point, it hangs right in balance. Another fascinating session of the day is up next. Stay tuned as the post-Tea session of Day 3 begins in just about 20 minutes.

Pakistan, meanwhile, struggled to make inroads. They turned to spin bowling from one end, hoping to find some turn, but to no avail. Abrar who bowled a lengthy spell was ineffective and found it challenging to trouble the well-set English batters, despite of some visible cracks on the surface. The pacers did manage to extract a hint of reverse swing, creating a few opportunities and ultimately claiming Duckett's wicket off Jamal's bowling. But, that was the only success for the home side in this session.

Although Duckett fell short of a well-deserved century, his brisk innings set a solid foundation. Harry Brook then joined Root at the crease, and together they maintained a healthy scoring rate, with only a minor dip. Root notched up another century to his name, his first on Pakistani soil while Brook shouldered him responsibly as well and stands unbeaten on 64.

The second session, widely regarded as the prime batting time of the day, saw England build on their earlier momentum. Ben Duckett and Joe Root crafted a pivotal partnership, amassing 136 runs from just 154 deliveries. Duckett expertly exploited all areas of the field, finding the boundary with regularity, while Root maintained his characteristic steady pace, punctuating his innings with some elegant drives.

TEA, DAY 3 - Session Summary - 25 overs, 119 runs, 1 wicket - Another session has flown by in this Test and even after 8 sessions of play, the track remains absolutely stubborn for the bowlers. England has managed to pile up a good amount of runs in this session as well and has made the Pakistani bowlers work extremely hard to get breakthroughs. England would be mighty pleased with the way they have batted as they walk in the sheds.

Duckett targeted Abrar Ahmed and hit him out of the attack after which the pacers tried to extract some reverse swing which really wasn't there and now a crucial session lies ahead for them where they might be forced to press the issue a bit more.

England began Day 3 with a well-set Zak Crawley and Joe Root at the crease and the former began proceedings in style with a flurry of boundaries. However, he threw his wicket away on 78 with Root going along nicely at the other end. Ben Duckett then came out and it felt like his thumb never got injured as he was positive right from the off and kept attacking the Pakistani bowlers. They have put on 119 runs in quick time and both will be looking for their tons after the break.

SESSION SUMMARY - 25 overs, 136 runs and 1 wicket. We are through the first session on Day 3 and still, the bat is ruling the ball as England have piled on quick runs in the session and have given themselves a great platform to bat for a few more sessions and breach Pakistan's score but there's still a long way to go as they are still 324 runs behind.

JUST IN - David Gower on-air informs that Ben Duckett is doing well now and will most probably come out to bat today. A huge positive news for the English camp. He was struck with a left thumb dislocation on Day 2 in the process of taking the catch at the first slip, and his left hand was strapped as well. He was seen doing the fitness drills and also played some football with his teammates before the start of the day.

As we look ahead to Day 3, the pitch remains largely favorable for batting, though some signs of wear have begun to appear. Late on Day 2, the ball showed hints of grip and turn, with occasional variable bounce as well, but that wasn't as threatening for the batters at all. The Bazballers will not flinch a bit from motoring the score at a good pace, being obedient to their new embraced strategy. Pakistan, on the other hand, will be eyeing the crucial first hour of play. They'll aim to exploit any early morning assistance and potentially variable conditions to make inroads. With both teams having clear objectives, we're set for a fascinating day of Test cricket. Stay tuned as the first ball of Day 3 isn't far away.

Pakistan, buoyed by their initial success, have since been met with resolute resistance. While Naseem and Shaheen posed threats in their opening spells, the pacers have found little assistance from the pitch. The spinners have shown glimpses of grip and turn, but Crawley, in particular, has taken an aggressive approach against Abrar. Pakistan has used four bowlers so far and only a spinner. Also, with the pitch expected to wear and tear in the remaining days, we might see more spin being deployed to ambush the English batters. But it remains to be seen how effective the bowlers can be on this flat track.

England faced an early setback with the loss of captain Ollie Pope for a duck, but Zak Crawley and Joe Root have since steadied the ship, scoring at a brisk pace and dampening Pakistan's hopes of a collapse. Their ability to navigate the critical first hour will be pivotal. There's also uncertainty surrounding Ben Duckett's possibility to come out to bat after he dislocated his left thumb, an unwelcome development for the English camp following their long stint in the field.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the third day of this first Test between Pakistan and England at Multan. It has been pretty much dominated by the batters so far and the pitch is still favourable for batting. After being toiled and sweated for almost two days with the ball, England has come up with a positive intent with the bat. Although, Pakistan has a huge cushion of lead at its disposal. This 'Moving Day' can shape the narrative of the game.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Well then, that's a wrap from Day 2. Pakistan has bossed up this match so far and would aim to continue this momentum. England, on the other hand, would be aiming to ascend with their little surge towards the backend with two well-established batters unbeaten on the crease. Day 3 is known as the 'Moving Day' in Test cricket by the pundits. So let us see how in whose favor it moves, and who dominates it. Do join us on 9th October for Day 3. The action will begin at 5 am GMT. But as you all know, you can join us an hour early for the build-up. Take care, ADIOS!

Aamer Jamal is down for a quick chat. He talks about the catch he took and says that he sets his mind every delivery, hoping that one might come his way. Adds that so far they have bowled stump-to stump which is the way to go and given the pitch is low and slow, they should bowl more into the pitch. Mentions that they will come with a good mindset on Day 3 morning and get a good first innings lead.

So whom does this day belong to? A silly question, eh? Well, Pakistan has made England field in the heat of Multan for almost six sessions - which is two whole days and have notched up above 500 runs - supported by three centurions, a fabulous 82 by Saud Shakeel, and handy contributions by the lower middle order as well.

Pakistan, replicating their batting performance, came out all guns blazing with the ball. Afridi and Naseem Shah troubled the English top order and constantly tried to create chances here and there with threatening spells in tandem. All in all, it was a job well done kind of a day for Pakistan first of course, with the bat, while they could have done much better with the ball.

Determined to erase memories of their lackluster bowling display, England's batters strode out with an aim to strike back hard. However, their resolve was immediately tested as skipper Ollie Pope fell early. However, the alliance between Zak Crawley and Joe Root eased things up a bit for England as the two constructed a productive partnership. The pitch was still flat and good for the batters to pile up runs and the two effectively dashed the hopes of a collapse to see England through the session.

The English attack endured a grueling ordeal, toiling for 149 long overs for almost two days under the unforgiving sun. Jack Leach emerged as the bright spot, snaring three wickets, while Atkinson and Carse managed two apiece. Yet, their efforts were marred by a couple of dropped chances late in the innings, adding to their frustration.

Pakistan decided to continue to bat after Tea. With the ball not doing much at all, they decided to come out with an aggressive intent.  Salman Agha and Shaheen Afridi, sensing the docile nature of the pitch, forged a blistering partnership of 85 runs off just 103 balls. Agha led the charge, crafting a masterful century, while Afridi provided crucial support with some lusty blows. Their efforts propelled Pakistan to a formidable 556, leaving England's bowlers battered and weary.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for the last hydration break of the second day! Despite being rocked very early into the innings, England looks settled as of now with Zak Crawley and Joe Root scoring runs at a brisk pace. Both have added 39 runs in just 52 deliveries so far. Pakistan on the other hand, have asked all the tough questions to the Pakistani top order with Naseem Shah removing Ollie Pope on a duck, courtesy of a screamer catch by Aamer Jamal. England's aim would be to go unblemished without further damage till the end of the day as the pitch is still flat and good to bat on with no visible swing at all.
